learningObjectives.title: Polar or coral environments and management

questions.q: Which large-scale global ecosystem is typically located around the Equator?
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests are found in a band around the Equator where it is consistently hot and wet.

questions.q: Why does heavy rainfall occur near the Equator?
options: Cold air sinks, creating high pressure
Warm air rises, cools and condenses, creating low pressure
Dry descending air prevents cloud formation
Ocean currents block moisture from the land
questions.explain: Intense heating at the Equator makes air rise, cool and condense, giving the low pressure and high rainfall of the rainforest belt.

questions.q: Hot deserts are mainly found at around which latitude?
questions.explain: At about 30 degrees dry air descends, creating high pressure and the arid conditions of hot deserts.

questions.q: Which of the following is a cold, treeless biome found at high latitudes?
questions.explain: Tundra is a cold biome of low-growing vegetation with permanently frozen ground beneath the surface.

questions.q: Which factor is the main influence on the global distribution of biomes?
questions.explain: Temperature and precipitation patterns, driven by climate, largely determine where each biome is located.

questions.q: A location at about 30 degrees north experiences dry, descending air and high pressure for most of the year. Which biome is most likely to be found there?
questions.explain: Descending dry air at around 30 degrees creates the arid high-pressure conditions typical of hot deserts.

questions.q: Roughly how much rain does a tropical rainforest typically receive each year?
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests are extremely wet, usually receiving well over 2000 mm of rainfall annually.

questions.q: Which best describes the temperature pattern of a tropical rainforest?
options: Cold all year, around 0 degrees C
Hot all year, around 27 degrees C
questions.explain: Rainforests stay hot with little seasonal variation, averaging around 26 to 28 degrees C throughout the year.

questions.q: What name is given to the tallest trees that poke out above the main rainforest canopy?
questions.explain: Emergents are the tallest trees that rise above the continuous canopy layer to reach maximum light.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the buttress roots found on many rainforest trees?
options: To store water during dry spells
To provide support for tall trees in thin, shallow soils
To defend the tree against animals
questions.explain: Large buttress roots stabilise very tall trees whose roots cannot go deep in the shallow rainforest soil.

questions.q: How do the drip tips found on many rainforest leaves help the plant?
options: They channel excess water off the leaf quickly
They reflect sunlight to prevent overheating
questions.explain: Pointed drip tips allow heavy rainfall to run off rapidly, preventing rot and fungal growth on the leaf.

questions.q: Rainforest soils, which are often deep red and infertile, are commonly known as what?
questions.explain: Tropical rainforest soils are latosols, which are typically deep, red and low in nutrients.

questions.q: Why are rainforest soils generally infertile despite the lush vegetation above them?
options: Most nutrients are stored in the vegetation and quickly recycled, while rain leaches nutrients from the soil
There is too little sunlight to warm the soil
The soil is too sandy to hold plants
questions.explain: Nutrients are held in the biomass and cycled rapidly, and heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil through leaching.

questions.q: A large area of the Amazon rainforest is cleared and replaced with grass to raise beef cattle. Which cause of deforestation does this show?
questions.explain: Clearing forest to graze cattle is cattle ranching, a leading cause of Amazon deforestation.

questions.q: Which is a likely global consequence of large-scale rainforest deforestation?
options: Increased carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and enhanced climate change
A fall in global sea levels
Cooler global temperatures due to more sunlight reflection
An increase in soil fertility worldwide
questions.explain: Removing trees releases stored carbon and reduces carbon uptake, adding to atmospheric CO2 and climate change.

questions.q: Which of the following is a sustainable way to manage a tropical rainforest?
options: Building new roads for open-cast mining
Draining and burning the forest floor
questions.explain: Selective logging with replanting removes only some trees and replaces them, allowing the forest to recover.

questions.q: A tour company brings small groups to a rainforest, employs local guides and uses profits to fund conservation. Which sustainable strategy is this?
questions.explain: Small-scale tourism that benefits local people and funds conservation is ecotourism, a sustainable management strategy.

questions.q: In which conditions do coral reefs grow best?
questions.explain: Reef-building corals thrive in warm, clear, shallow tropical water where sunlight can reach them.

questions.q: What happens during coral bleaching?
options: Coral polyps grow a thicker protective shell
Coral expels its algae (zooxanthellae), loses colour and may die
Coral produces more colourful pigments to attract fish
Coral reproduces rapidly to form new reefs
questions.explain: Stress, often from warmer seas, makes coral expel its symbiotic zooxanthellae, turning it white and threatening its survival.

questions.q: Which statement best describes precipitation in polar environments such as Antarctica?
options: Very low precipitation, making them cold deserts
Moderate rainfall spread evenly through the year
questions.explain: Polar regions receive very little precipitation and are classed as cold deserts despite being covered in ice.
